fields.title: 2. Competition — Vulcan LV-01 Launch Failure (Amazon Leo)
fields.md:
| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Status | 'Launch Failure' — the launch vehicle did not reach orbit, or the payload did not separate · failreason blank | ④ [LL2 launch record](https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/ef9850ad-1096-425b-9d27-f7bbd186e61a/) |
| Launch | 2026-11-15 17:40:30 UTC · SLC-41 (Cape Canaveral) | Same as above |
| Last updated | 2026-11-15 19:30:04 UTC · update at 18:32 UTC: 'orbit not reached, anomaly around T+10 minutes' | Same as above |
| ULA statement | About 50 minutes after launch: 'An anomaly occurred 10 minutes into the flight, and we were unable to place the Amazon mission into orbit.' There is not yet any specific data on the cause | ⑥ [Spaceflight Now 11/15](https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/11/15/ula-suffers-first-total-mission-failure-with-loss-of-vulcan-rocket-carrying-40-amazon-leo-satellites/) |
| Payload | 40 satellites — the first flight of the 38 Vulcan launches Amazon bought. Had it succeeded, cumulative Amazon Leo launches would have reached 436 satellites | Same as above |
| Significance | The first total failure since ULA was founded in 2006, and Vulcan's first flight in 9 months. Bloomberg reported that the first total mission loss set back the Starlink challenge | Same as above · ⑤ [Bloomberg 11/15](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-15/ula-vulcan-rocket-launches-with-its-first-amazon-leo-payload) |
| Amazon's other launch bookings | New Glenn 24 · Ariane 6 24 · Falcon 9 13. New Glenn has not yet returned to flight after the May launch pad explosion | ⑥ Spaceflight Now 11/15 |

- **Satellite count reconciliation**: The '45' in the LL2 mission description is generic wording used for Vulcan missions. This flight carried 40 satellites (Spaceflight Now · a report relaying ULA's October announcement). We adopt 40 (source: the two above).
- **T4** (Amazon Leo US consumer launch and pricing): This failure slowed deployment. However, T4 is judged by the posting of pricing and regions, so its status is 'Pending'. The remaining checkpoints are Ariane 64 LE-04 (11/23) · the 12/01 monthly · 2027-01-04 (source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T4]`).
- **R5** (no Kuiper US consumer plan launched by end of 2027 → base +5): This rule is judged only by whether the launch occurs. A launch failure is not a triggering event → **not triggered**. Conditions set before the outcome are not stretched to fit the event (source: `state.probability_adjustment_rules` R5).
- **T13** (diversification of defense launch supply): The Space Force had already put Vulcan national security launches on hold until further analysis is complete. There is no official announcement on how this failure affects the hold or NSSL assignments. Inputs are taken only from Space Force announcements and contract notices (source: Spaceflight Now 11/15 · `state.triggers_next_12m[T13]`).
